cited_details.statement: Recommender systems play a pivotal role in delivering personalized recommendations across various domains, from e-commerce to content streaming platforms [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

Pre-trained language models such as BERT and GPT learn general text representations and encode extensive world knowledge, enabling them to efficiently and accurately adapt to various downstream tasks [https://www.amazon.science/publications/language-models-as-recommender-systems-evaluations-and-limitations].

Large language models have demonstrated remarkable performance across diverse domains, prompting researchers to explore their potential for use in recommendation systems [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].

Recommender systems are renowned for their effectiveness and proficiency within clearly defined domains but are limited in adaptability and incapable of providing recommendations for unexplored data [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].
Large language models exhibit contextual awareness and strong adaptability to unseen data [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

Combining recommender systems and large language models creates a powerful tool for delivering contextual and relevant recommendations, even in cold scenarios characterized by high data sparsity [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].

The Retrieval-augmented Recommender System (RA-RS) approach combines the strengths of retrieval-based and generation-based models to enhance the ability of recommender systems to provide relevant suggestions [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608889].
Recommender systems have witnessed significant advancements and played an essential role in people's daily applications [http://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13366].

The Pretrain, Personalized Prompt, and Predict (P5) paradigm unifies multiple recommendation tasks that typically require task-specific architectures and training objectives [http://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13366].
P5 is referred to as Recommendation as Language Processing (RLP) [http://arxiv.org/abs/2203.13366].
VIP5 extends the recommendation-as-language-processing paradigm toward multimodal foundation models for recommendation [https://doi.org/10.18653/v1/2023.findings-emnlp.644].

Initial attempts to use LLMs for recommendation have leveraged rich knowledge and strong generalization through in-context learning by phrasing the recommendation task as prompts [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].

The performance of LLMs in recommendation tasks remains suboptimal due to a substantial disparity between the training tasks for LLMs and recommendation tasks, as well as inadequate recommendation data during pre-training [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].
TALLRec is an efficient and effective tuning framework for aligning large language models with recommendation data [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].

TALLRec can significantly enhance the recommendation capabilities of LLMs in the movie and book domains, even with a limited dataset of fewer than 100 samples [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].
The TALLRec framework is highly efficient and can be executed on a single RTX 3090 with LLaMA-7B [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].
The fine-tuned LLM in TALLRec exhibits robust cross-domain generalization [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608857].
LLM-Rec performs personalized recommendation via prompting large language models, leveraging keywords in original item descriptions [http://arxiv.org/abs/2307.15780].
With the explosive growth of commercial applications of recommender systems, multi-scenario recommendation has attracted considerable attention [https://doi.org/10.1145/3539618.3591750].
Multi-scenario recommendation utilizes data from multiple domains to improve their recommendation performance simultaneously [https://doi.org/10.1145/3539618.3591750].

PLATE is a prompt-enhanced paradigm for multi-scenario recommendation that first pre-trains a unified deep recommender backbone using data from all domains to capture the commonality across domains [https://doi.org/10.1145/3539618.3591750].
PLATE then conducts prompt tuning with two prompt modules that capture the distinctions among various domains and users [https://doi.org/10.1145/3539618.3591750].
PLATE demonstrates great compatibility with various deep recommender system backbone models and high computational efficiency [https://doi.org/10.1145/3539618.3591750].

Heterogeneous Knowledge Fusion extracts and fuses heterogeneous knowledge from user heterogeneous behavior information to address feature sparsity and knowledge fragmentation issues [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608874].

Heterogeneous Knowledge Fusion performs instruction tuning on the LLM by combining heterogeneous knowledge and recommendation tasks, and its method effectively integrates user heterogeneous behavior and significantly improves recommendation performance [https://doi.org/10.1145/3604915.3608874].
CLLM4Rec is the first generative recommender system that tightly integrates the LLM paradigm and ID paradigm of recommender systems [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].
CLLM4Rec extends the vocabulary of pretrained LLMs with user and item ID tokens to faithfully model user and item collaborative and content semantics [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

CLLM4Rec introduces a soft-plus-hard prompting strategy that uses a prompt consisting of heterogeneous soft user and item tokens and hard vocab tokens, together with a main text consisting of homogeneous item tokens or vocab tokens [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].

CLLM4Rec introduces a mutual regularization strategy to address issues such as spuriously correlated user and item descriptors, ineffective language modeling on user and item data, and inefficient auto-regressive recommendations [https://doi.org/10.1145/3589334.3645347].
TASTE verbalizes items and user-item interactions using identifiers and attributes of items and recommends items by matching their text representations [https://doi.org/10.1145/3583780.3615077].

TASTE additionally proposes an attention sparsity method that enables it to model longer user-item interactions by reducing the self-attention computations during encoding [https://doi.org/10.1145/3583780.3615077].
TASTE significantly improves recommendation accuracy by reducing the popularity bias of previous item-ID-based recommendation models [https://doi.org/10.1145/3583780.3615077].

TASTE alleviates the cold start problem by representing long-tail items using full-text modeling and bringing the benefits of pretrained language models to recommendation systems [https://doi.org/10.1145/3583780.3615077].
